<input_guardrails>
<!-- @skill-include: start input_guardrails | hash:957e7f01 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/input_guardrails.md -->
## Pre-Execution Guardrails (mechanized)

Run only if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob guardrails.input.enabled false` prints `true`
and env `LOA_GUARDRAILS_ENABLED` is not `false`: write the prompt/args to a temp file (Write tool), then run
`.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh --skill auditing-security --mode ${LOA_RUN_MODE:-interactive} --file <temp-file>`

| Outcome | Action |
|---------|--------|
| JSON `action: "BLOCK"` | HALT; report the script's `reason` to the user |
| JSON `action: "PROCEED"` or `"WARN"` | Continue (the script logs) |
| Script missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output | Continue (fail-open) |

Never pass prompt text as a bash argv (quote-blindness FP class) — always via `--file`.
<!-- @skill-include: end input_guardrails -->
</input_guardrails>

# Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor

<objective>
Audit code, architecture, infrastructure or sprint implementations for security and quality; produce prioritized findings with actionable remediation at the output path for the audit type.
</objective>

<zone_constraints>
## Zone Constraints

Three-Zone Model per CLAUDE.loa.md: `.claude/` system = never edit (use `.claude/overrides/` or `.loa.config.yaml`); `grimoires/loa/`, `.beads/` state = read/write; this skill's app zone (`src/`, `lib/`, `app/`) = **Read-only**.

Scope: app-zone files less the `.reviewignore` patterns (read it); `.claude/`, `grimoires/`, `.beads/` and `.run/` are excluded unless `--no-reviewignore` is passed.
</zone_constraints>

<integrity_precheck>
<!-- @skill-include: start integrity_precheck | hash:47b71a70 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/integrity_precheck.md -->
## Integrity Pre-Check (MANDATORY)

Before ANY operation, verify System Zone integrity:

1. Check config: read `integrity_enforcement` in `.loa.config.yaml`
2. If `strict` and drift detected -> **HALT** and report
3. If `warn` -> Log warning and proceed with caution
<!-- @skill-include: end integrity_precheck -->
</integrity_precheck>

<factual_grounding>
<!-- @skill-include: start factual_grounding | hash:edec7c58 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/factual_grounding.md -->
## Factual Grounding (MANDATORY)

Before ANY synthesis, planning, or recommendation:

1. **Extract quotes**: Pull word-for-word text from source files
2. **Cite explicitly**: `"[exact quote]" (file.md:L45)`
3. **Flag assumptions**: Prefix ungrounded claims with `[ASSUMPTION]`

**Grounded Example:**
```
The SDD specifies "PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector extension" (sdd.md:L123)
```

**Ungrounded Example:**
```
[ASSUMPTION] The database likely needs connection pooling
```
<!-- @skill-include: end factual_grounding -->
</factual_grounding>

<context_discipline>
<!-- @skill-include: start context_discipline | hash:8b81d75a | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/context_discipline.md -->
## Context Discipline

Class: `.run/context-class` (`long` default; `standard` via `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=standard` or a
≤200K model). `.claude/protocols/tool-result-clearing.md` — long 20K/50K/30K/150K, standard 2K/5K/3K/15K (single /
accumulated / full file / session) → extract ≤10 files, ≤20 words, file:line to NOTES.md; reason
from it. Big files: `notes-guard.sh read --file F --section <H>` / `--index` first. Start: NOTES.md
"Session Continuity"; end / pre-compaction: update it.
<!-- @skill-include: end context_discipline -->
</context_discipline>

<trajectory_logging>
<!-- @skill-include: start trajectory_logging | hash:e809010f | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/trajectory_logging.md -->
## Trajectory Logging

Log each significant step to `grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory/{agent}-{date}.jsonl`:

```json
{"timestamp": "...", "agent": "...", "action": "...", "reasoning": "...", "grounding": {...}}
```
<!-- @skill-include: end trajectory_logging -->
</trajectory_logging>

<grounding_requirements>
Read the actual implementation (never documentation alone) and cross-reference the technical-debt registry if one exists. Every finding cites the CWE/OWASP/CVE it violates with an absolute URL (not just the name) and quotes the vulnerable code inline. Where purpose or trust context (internal vs external) is unclear, state the assumption; say "Unable to assess" for obfuscated or inaccessible code and record scope limits in the report.
</grounding_requirements>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

<parallel_execution>
## Parallel Splitting (large scopes)

When splitting, use 5 parallel Explore agents — one per category (Security / Architecture / Code Quality / DevOps / Blockchain-Crypto) — each scoped to its category's files and returning findings with severity, file:line, and remediation (per-category file globs and prompts: see `resources/PARALLEL-SPLIT.md`). Consolidate: deduplicate overlaps, sort CRITICAL → LOW, take the overall risk from the highest severity present.
</parallel_execution>

<rubric_scoring>
## Rubric-Based Scoring

Score each dimension 1–5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md` (Security weighted highest; Blockchain when applicable), recording the findings that justify each score.
</rubric_scoring>

<structured_output>
## Structured JSONL Output

Alongside the markdown report, write machine-parseable findings to `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/findings.jsonl` per `resources/OUTPUT-SCHEMA.md` (the schema, each `reasoning_trace`, the closing summary record).
</structured_output>

<communication_style>
Be direct and specific, with evidence: "Line 47: user input passed unsanitized to eval(). Critical RCE. OWASP A03." — never "the code has security issues". Document blast radius, prioritize by exploitability and impact, suggest pragmatic fixes, and never defer a critical issue.
</communication_style>

<documentation_audit>
## Documentation Audit

For sprint audits, confirm each task has a documentation-coherence report (Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-task-*.md`; sprint level: `documentation-coherence-sprint-*.md`) or was manually verified — checks and red-flag tables: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation. Blockers: an unverified missing report; uncommented security-critical code; a CHANGELOG omitting security changes; secrets or internal URLs in docs or comments; auth/crypto changes without security documentation; API changes that don't match the endpoint docs.
</documentation_audit>

<checklists>
Complete checklists for the five categories (Security, Architecture, Code Quality, DevOps, Blockchain/Crypto): `resources/REFERENCE.md`. Immediate CRITICAL red flags: private keys in code, SQL via string concatenation, user input to eval(), empty catch blocks on security code, hardcoded secrets.
</checklists>

<beads_workflow>
With `br` installed: `resources/BEADS-WORKFLOW.md` (sync, the audit comment, the `security*` labels, a discovered vulnerability).
</beads_workflow>

<retrospective_postlude>
<!-- @skill-include: start retrospective_postlude | hash:53d44248 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md -->
After the main skill logic, if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled`
prints `true` (and `invisible_retrospective.skills` does not disable this skill), silently run the
learning-signal scan per `.claude/skills/continuous-learning/SKILL.md` and its
`resources/RETROSPECTIVE.md` (quality gates, sanitization, trajectory logging). Never when the
active skill is continuous-learning itself.

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

<parallel_execution>
## Parallel Splitting (large scopes)

When splitting, use 5 parallel Explore agents — one per category (Security / Architecture / Code Quality / DevOps / Blockchain-Crypto) — each scoped to its category's files and returning findings with severity, file:line, and remediation (per-category file globs and prompts: see `resources/PARALLEL-SPLIT.md`). Consolidate: deduplicate overlaps, sort CRITICAL → LOW, take the overall risk from the highest severity present.
</parallel_execution>

<rubric_scoring>
## Rubric-Based Scoring

Score each dimension 1–5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md` (Security weighted highest; Blockchain when applicable), recording the findings that justify each score.
</rubric_scoring>

<structured_output>
## Structured JSONL Output

Alongside the markdown report, write machine-parseable findings to `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/findings.jsonl` per `resources/OUTPUT-SCHEMA.md` (the schema, each `reasoning_trace`, the closing summary record).
</structured_output>

<communication_style>
Be direct and specific, with evidence: "Line 47: user input passed unsanitized to eval(). Critical RCE. OWASP A03." — never "the code has security issues". Document blast radius, prioritize by exploitability and impact, suggest pragmatic fixes, and never defer a critical issue.
</communication_style>

<documentation_audit>
## Documentation Audit

For sprint audits, confirm each task has a documentation-coherence report (Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-task-*.md`; sprint level: `documentation-coherence-sprint-*.md`) or was manually verified — checks and red-flag tables: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation. Blockers: an unverified missing report; uncommented security-critical code; a CHANGELOG omitting security changes; secrets or internal URLs in docs or comments; auth/crypto changes without security documentation; API changes that don't match the endpoint docs.
</documentation_audit>

<checklists>
Complete checklists for the five categories (Security, Architecture, Code Quality, DevOps, Blockchain/Crypto): `resources/REFERENCE.md`. Immediate CRITICAL red flags: private keys in code, SQL via string concatenation, user input to eval(), empty catch blocks on security code, hardcoded secrets.
</checklists>

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff`: a new `red-test-check.sh`, a `--type glossary` validator plus a date-gated `### Seams Under Test` rule in `validate-artifact.sh`, `tools/check-glossary-terms.sh` with a CI workflow, two glossaries, an allowlist, fixtures, four bats suites and prose edits to six skill files; three mount lists gain `.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md`.

What is good: the code was verified, not just read. In a scratch tree with the PR applied (mawk 1.3.4, bash 5.2, git worktrees), all four new suites pass — `glossary-terms` 20/20, `glossary-validator` 19/19, `sprint-seams` 10/10 (SEAMS-8 skips by design outside the cycle-128 checkout), `red-test-check` 17/17. `tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --report` passes on the live kernel (16 tokens kept, 0 missing), both glossaries validate clean, the cycle-127 fixture gains only the WARN the test expects, the pinned `actions/checkout` SHA is genuinely v4.3.1, the three mount/gitignore lists are consistent, argv-injection guards on `--red/--green/--test-file` work (RTC-12), and the honest-scope header of `red-test-check.sh` is a model of saying what a check does not prove.

What blocks: one HIGH, reproduced. `red-test-check.sh` symlinks the live tree's `node_modules`/`.venv`/`vendor`/`target`/`.tox` into both worktrees by default. For the two most common layouts those directories carry absolute back-references into the live tree (a Python editable install's `.pth`, npm/pnpm workspace links), so the "red" and "green" runs both execute the live working copy, not `RED_SHA`/`GREEN_SHA`. Reproduced here with a real venv: a correct failing-test-then-fix pair reports `DECOY` (exit 3) and prints `pkg imported from <live tree>/src/pkg/__init__.py`; with `--no-link-deps` the interpreter is absent and it reports `NOT_A_RED` (exit 127). The reviewing skill tells the reviewer to cite this output as proof of "Test fails with current code", so the gate can certify a red-before-green that never ran. The fix is small (opt-in linking, or refuse to link a directory with back-references, or verify the resolved module path lies inside the worktree).

Five MEDIUM and ten LOW observations follow, including three demonstrated by running the code (noexec `TMPDIR` → false `NOT_A_RED`; "e.g." counted as a sentence; a non-ISO header date silently downgrades the seams rule to WARN). The cross-model dissent produced 7 findings (3 marked BLOCKING); triage below adopts one as the HIGH above, downgrades three to MEDIUM with reasons, folds two, and refutes one half with evidence.

`reviewer.md` carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough; per `pr/REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md` there is no implementation report in this frozen evaluation and that pre-flight is skipped rather than applied as an automatic fail. The verdict rests on the HIGH.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Functionality / correctness of the red-before-green gate

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:222-227` — `link_deps` symlinks the live tree's dependency directories (`DEP_DIRS`, line 47) into the red and green worktrees by default; when such a directory carries an absolute back-reference to the live tree, both runs test the live working copy instead of the two commits, and the verdict is wrong.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:222-227` (also `:47`, `:346`)
**Issue:** A Python editable install (`pip install -e .`, PEP 660) writes a `.pth`/finder into `.venv/.../site-packages` that resolves `import pkg` to the live tree's absolute `src/` path; npm/pnpm/yarn workspaces place `node_modules/@scope/pkg -> ../../packages/pkg` links that resolve relative to the live `node_modules`. Linked into a worktree, `.venv/bin/python` (or `node`) in the red worktree imports the live tree's code. Reproduced in this review with a real venv and an `__editable__.pkg.pth` pointing at `<repo>/src`, red commit = failing test + buggy `add`, green = fixed `add`, live tree = green:
```
$ red-test-check.sh --red $RED -- .venv/bin/python tests/test_add.py
red-test-check: the test passes at the red commit: it does not reproduce the bug
red-test-check: red f37f831c exit 0; green 48fa83d4 exit 0; linked deps: .venv
pkg imported from /home/evaluser/rr/fx2/src/pkg/__init__.py
verdict: DECOY            (exit 3)
$ red-test-check.sh --red $RED --no-link-deps -- .venv/bin/python tests/test_add.py
red-test-check: the red run exited 127 (command not found or not executable)
verdict: NOT_A_RED        (exit 4)
```
**Why This Matters:** The script's purpose (header lines 3-18) is to prove "red fails by assertion and green passes"; here a correct red-before-green is reported as a decoy, and a live tree that differs from either commit yields arbitrary `VERIFIED`/`DECOY` mixes (a fix commit that also edits the test can read `VERIFIED` while the source change was never exercised). `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:219` instructs the reviewer to run this and "cite its output for 'Test fails with current code'", and `head/.claude/skills/bug-triaging/resources/templates/micro-sprint.md:43` makes exit 0 an acceptance criterion, so the error propagates into gate decisions. The header (lines 27-30) warns only that writes land in the live copy, not that the code under test can be the live tree. Neither default has a working path for the standard Python `src/` layout.
**Required Fix:** Make linking opt-in (`--link-deps`) with `--setup` as the documented way to install into the worktree, or keep the default but refuse to link a directory that carries back-references (any `*.pth`/`__editable__*` under a linked `site-packages`; any symlink inside `node_modules` whose target lies outside it; any `vendor`/`target` that is itself a symlink), with a clear message naming the directory; alternatively, after linking, resolve the package under test (`python -c 'import pkg; print(pkg.__file__)'`-style probe, or `node -p "require.resolve(...)"`) and fail closed with a distinct verdict when the path is outside the worktree. Add RTC cases for an editable `.pth` and a workspace symlink proving the refusal, and state the limitation in the header and in `micro-sprint.md:43`.
**Reference:** CWE-706 (use of incorrectly-resolved name or reference); SDD D-7.5..D-7.7 as cited by the script header (the SDD itself is not in this workspace).

Non-blocking. Severities are the damage if the scenario happens; confidence is how sure I am that it does.

### 1. red-test-check.sh robustness

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:183` — the worktrees live under `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/..."`; on a host whose temp filesystem is mounted `noexec` (this sandbox's `/tmp` is), a test command that is a script inside the tree (`-- ./run-tests.sh`, `-- scripts/test`) exits 126 at both commits and the gate reports `NOT_A_RED` for a legitimate red.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:183` (classification at `:326`)
**Suggestion:** Create the scratch directory under the repository (`$MAIN/.git/red-test-check.XXXXXX` or `$MAIN/.run/`) with `TMPDIR` as the fallback, or honour a dedicated override; when a run exits 126 and the tail contains `Permission denied`, name the probable cause in the message. **File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:222-227` (also `:47`, `:346`)

Linked into a worktree, `.venv/bin/python` (or `node`) in the red worktree imports the live tree's code. red-test-check: the red run exited 127 (command not found or not executable)
verdict: NOT_A_RED        (exit 4)

content.content:
## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff`: a new `red-test-check.sh`, a `--type glossary` validator plus a date-gated `### Seams Under Test` rule in `validate-artifact.sh`, `tools/check-glossary-terms.sh` with a CI workflow, two glossaries, an allowlist, fixtures, four bats suites and prose edits to six skill files; three mount lists gain `.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md`.

What is good: the code was verified, not just read. In a scratch tree with the PR applied (mawk 1.3.4, bash 5.2, git worktrees), all four new suites pass — `glossary-terms` 20/20, `glossary-validator` 19/19, `sprint-seams` 10/10 (SEAMS-8 skips by design outside the cycle-128 checkout), `red-test-check` 17/17. `tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --report` passes on the live kernel (16 tokens kept, 0 missing), both glossaries validate clean, the cycle-127 fixture gains only the WARN the test expects, the pinned `actions/checkout` SHA is genuinely v4.3.1, the three mount/gitignore lists are consistent, argv-injection guards on `--red/--green/--test-file` work (RTC-12), and the honest-scope header of `red-test-check.sh` is a model of saying what a check does not prove.

What blocks: one HIGH, reproduced. `red-test-check.sh` symlinks the live tree's `node_modules`/`.venv`/`vendor`/`target`/`.tox` into both worktrees by default. For the two most common layouts those directories carry absolute back-references into the live tree (a Python editable install's `.pth`, npm/pnpm workspace links), so the "red" and "green" runs both execute the live working copy, not `RED_SHA`/`GREEN_SHA`. Reproduced here with a real venv: a correct failing-test-then-fix pair reports `DECOY` (exit 3) and prints `pkg imported from <live tree>/src/pkg/__init__.py`; with `--no-link-deps` the interpreter is absent and it reports `NOT_A_RED` (exit 127). The reviewing skill tells the reviewer to cite this output as proof of "Test fails with current code", so the gate can certify a red-before-green that never ran. The fix is small (opt-in linking, or refuse to link a directory with back-references, or verify the resolved module path lies inside the worktree).

Five MEDIUM and ten LOW observations follow, including three demonstrated by running the code (noexec `TMPDIR` → false `NOT_A_RED`; "e.g." counted as a sentence; a non-ISO header date silently downgrades the seams rule to WARN). The cross-model dissent produced 7 findings (3 marked BLOCKING); triage below adopts one as the HIGH above, downgrades three to MEDIUM with reasons, folds two, and refutes one half with evidence.

`reviewer.md` carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough; per `pr/REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md` there is no implementation report in this frozen evaluation and that pre-flight is skipped rather than applied as an automatic fail. The verdict rests on the HIGH.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Functionality / correctness of the red-before-green gate

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:222-227` — `link_deps` symlinks the live tree's dependency directories (`DEP_DIRS`, line 47) into the red and green worktrees by default; when such a directory carries an absolute back-reference to the live tree, both runs test the live working copy instead of the two commits, and the verdict is wrong.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:222-227` (also `:47`, `:346`)
**Issue:** A Python editable install (`pip install -e .`, PEP 660) writes a `.pth`/finder into `.venv/.../site-packages` that resolves `import pkg` to the live tree's absolute `src/` path; npm/pnpm/yarn workspaces place `node_modules/@scope/pkg -> ../../packages/pkg` links that resolve relative to the live `node_modules`. Linked into a worktree, `.venv/bin/python` (or `node`) in the red worktree imports the live tree's code. Reproduced in this review with a real venv and an `__editable__.pkg.pth` pointing at `<repo>/src`, red commit = failing test + buggy `add`, green = fixed `add`, live tree = green:
```
$ red-test-check.sh --red $RED -- .venv/bin/python tests/test_add.py
red-test-check: the test passes at the red commit: it does not reproduce the bug
red-test-check: red f37f831c exit 0; green 48fa83d4 exit 0; linked deps: .venv
pkg imported from /home/evaluser/rr/fx2/src/pkg/__init__.py
verdict: DECOY            (exit 3)
$ red-test-check.sh --red $RED --no-link-deps -- .venv/bin/python tests/test_add.py
red-test-check: the red run exited 127 (command not found or not executable)
verdict: NOT_A_RED        (exit 4)
```
**Why This Matters:** The script's purpose (header lines 3-18) is to prove "red fails by assertion and green passes"; here a correct red-before-green is reported as a decoy, and a live tree that differs from either commit yields arbitrary `VERIFIED`/`DECOY` mixes (a fix commit that also edits the test can read `VERIFIED` while the source change was never exercised). `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:219` instructs the reviewer to run this and "cite its output for 'Test fails with current code'", and `head/.claude/skills/bug-triaging/resources/templates/micro-sprint.md:43` makes exit 0 an acceptance criterion, so the error propagates into gate decisions. The header (lines 27-30) warns only that writes land in the live copy, not that the code under test can be the live tree. Neither default has a working path for the standard Python `src/` layout.
**Required Fix:** Make linking opt-in (`--link-deps`) with `--setup` as the documented way to install into the worktree, or keep the default but refuse to link a directory that carries back-references (any `*.pth`/`__editable__*` under a linked `site-packages`; any symlink inside `node_modules` whose target lies outside it; any `vendor`/`target` that is itself a symlink), with a clear message naming the directory; alternatively, after linking, resolve the package under test (`python -c 'import pkg; print(pkg.__file__)'`-style probe, or `node -p "require.resolve(...)"`) and fail closed with a distinct verdict when the path is outside the worktree. Add RTC cases for an editable `.pth` and a workspace symlink proving the refusal, and state the limitation in the header and in `micro-sprint.md:43`.
**Reference:** CWE-706 (use of incorrectly-resolved name or reference); SDD D-7.5..D-7.7 as cited by the script header (the SDD itself is not in this workspace).

---

## Observations

Non-blocking. Severities are the damage if the scenario happens; confidence is how sure I am that it does.

### 1. red-test-check.sh robustness

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:183` — the worktrees live under `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/..."`; on a host whose temp filesystem is mounted `noexec` (this sandbox's `/tmp` is), a test command that is a script inside the tree (`-- ./run-tests.sh`, `-- scripts/test`) exits 126 at both commits and the gate reports `NOT_A_RED` for a legitimate red.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:183` (classification at `:326`)
**Suggestion:** Create the scratch directory under the repository (`$MAIN/.git/red-test-check.XXXXXX` or `$MAIN/.run/`) with `TMPDIR` as the fallback, or honour a dedicated override; when a run exits 126 and the tail contains `Permission denied`, name the probable cause in the message. Reproduced: `TMPDIR=/tmp red-test-check.sh --red $RED -- ./run-tests.sh` → `timeout: failed to run command './run-tests.sh': Permission denied`, `verdict: NOT_A_RED`, exit 4; the same pair with an exec-capable `TMPDIR` → `VERIFIED`.
**Benefit:** No false blocks on hardened CI runners and containers.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/skills/bug-triaging/resources/templates/micro-sprint.md:43` — the new acceptance criterion reads "does not weaken the test (`red-test-check.sh …` exits 0)", but a green commit that only rewrites the test to pass is a stderr `WARN` with exit 0 (`head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:180`; RTC-14 at `head/tests/unit/red-test-check.bats:238` asserts exactly this), and `--json` (`:135-145`) carries no `warnings` field at all, so a machine consumer never sees it.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/bug-triaging/resources/templates/micro-sprint.md:43`, `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:180`, `:135`
**Suggestion:** Either give the test-only case its own verdict and exit code (e.g. `TEST_ONLY`, exit 6) so the AC "exits 0" means what it says, or add `warnings: [...]` to the JSON object and reword the AC to "exits 0 and the reviewer confirms the red test is unchanged at green". The path-based check is also defeated by a fix commit that touches any non-test file (a comment), which the header should say.
**Benefit:** The AC stops over-claiming; `--json` consumers (run mode, graders) get the signal.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:52-70` — `NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS` covers pytest collection/import errors (`:61-62`) but not pytest setup errors (`ERROR at setup`, `fixture 'x' not found`), unittest's loader (`Failed to import test module`), or jest's `Test suite failed to run`; a red whose test never reached its assertion because a fixture was missing reads as an assertion failure, and a green that adds the fixture reads `VERIFIED`. (Dissent DISS-001; downgraded from BLOCKING: the header states the honest scope and the reviewer still reads the test, and the listed runners' most common classes are covered.)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:52-70`
**Suggestion:** Add the three patterns above (one entry per runner, as the comment at `:49-50` asks) with RTC cases, and prefer structured results where cheap (pytest `--junitxml`/`-rA` summary line, `go test -json`) so "error" and "fail" are told apart by the runner, not by grep.
**Benefit:** Fewer false reds accepted as reproduction.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:270-277` and `:198-205` — on the no-`timeout` path the watcher's `TERM → sleep 2 → KILL` escalation (`:256-262`) is cancelled: `wait "$RUN_PID"` returns as soon as the direct child dies from the TERM and the script immediately `kill`s the watcher (`:275`) before its KILL reaches the group, so a grandchild that ignores TERM survives (the header at `:33-34` promises "TERM, then KILL after 2 s"). On every path, `cleanup` (`:198-205`) sends one TERM and proceeds straight to `worktree remove --force` and the scratch-directory removal without waiting or escalating. (Dissent DISS-002 and DISS-C-004 folded; downgraded: requires a TERM-ignoring descendant and, for the first, a host without `timeout`/`gtimeout` — e.g. stock macOS.)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:270-277`, `:198-205`
**Suggestion:** In `run_bounded`, when `$flag` exists let the watcher finish (wait for it) before clearing; in `cleanup`, after TERM poll `kill -0` for ≤2 s, then send KILL to the group, `wait` it, and run `worktree prune` a second time after the scratch directory is gone so a failed `remove` is still pruned.
**Benefit:** No orphaned processes writing into removed directories or into linked live-tree dependency directories.

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:216` — `git worktree add --detach` does not initialise submodules; in a consumer project mounted in submodule mode the worktree's `.loa/` is empty and every manifest symlink under `.claude/` dangles, so a test that sources a framework script fails identically at red and green (`GREEN_FAILS`, exit 1) with no hint of the cause and no `NOT_A_RED` pattern matching "No such file or directory". (Dissent DISS-C-005.)
**Suggestion:** After `worktree add`, `git -C "$path" submodule update --init --recursive` when `.gitmodules` exists, or link the live `.loa` the way dependencies are linked; add the `.claude/…: No such file or directory` shape to the heuristics.

### 2. validate-artifact.sh

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1297` — the sentence counter `gsub(/[.!?]+[)"]*[[:space:]]/ …)` counts abbreviations: `**Probe**: A check, e.g. a smoke test. It is cheap.` is rejected as "has 3 sentences; at most two" (reproduced). Common in definitions ("e.g.", "i.e.", "vs.", "etc. ").
**Suggestion:** Exclude a short lowercase token before the period (`(^|[[:space:]])(e\.g|i\.e|etc|vs)\.` → neutralise first), or count only `[.!?] +[A-Z]` boundaries.

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:871` — the seams gate keys on the first `**Date:**` line parsed as `YYYY-MM-DD`; a header such as `**Date:** October 14, 2026` is read as undated and the hard rule silently degrades to the WARN (reproduced: `WARN: undated plan …`, exit 0). A hard gate should not be bypassable by date spelling.
**Suggestion:** When a `**Date:**` line exists but no ISO date parses, emit a violation ("header date must be YYYY-MM-DD") or treat the plan as dated today; the template (`sprint-template.md:4`) can state the format.

- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:867` — `SEAMS_REQUIRED_FROM="2026-10-13"` is a week before this merge; any plan authored in that window without the block hard-fails when re-validated after a framework bump, with no migration path but editing the plan. (Dissent DISS-C-003(b).) Its part (a), that `/bug` micro-sprints fail out of the box, is refuted: `micro-sprint.md` has no `**Date:**` header (undated → WARN) and `/bug` validates with `--type bug-triage` on `triage.md` (`bug-triaging/SKILL.md:381`); no script in `.claude/scripts` or `.claude/hooks` runs `--type sprint`, only the `/sprint-plan` skill does.
**Suggestion:** Either accept as intended (the cycle-128 plan is the first required one) and say so in the CHANGELOG, or gate on a template-version marker in the plan header rather than a date.

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1253` — `SIMPLICITY[shrink]` note only: `validate_glossary` is ~74 lines, one awk program with 15 rules; it mirrors the sibling validators (`validate_spike`, `validate_sprint_deferred`) and reads top-down, so this is accepted with that justification. Over-engineering pass otherwise: Lean already. Ship.

### 3. Permissions, CI, docs

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:6` (and `:27`) — `Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh *)` is added to the review role's allowed tools; everything after `--` (and `--setup`) is exec'd verbatim in two worktrees, so the glob grants a role whose stated boundary is "State-Zone feedback/checkmarks only" (`:7`) arbitrary command execution, and with dependencies linked (see the Changes Required entry) write access to the live tree's `node_modules`/`.venv`/`target`. The test command is taken from `reviewer.md` / the micro-sprint plan, which the engineer agent writes, so engineer-side content steers what the reviewer runs (CWE-78 class via prompt content). (Dissent DISS-C-002.)
**Suggestion:** Allowlist runner basenames in the script (`bats`, `pytest`, `python -m pytest`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `cargo`, `go`, `sh <in-tree file>`) with an explicit `--allow-any-command` for the implement role, or read the command from committed config (`.loa.config.yaml` test runner) and refuse ad-hoc argv in review mode; at minimum document the widened surface in the skill's zone comment at `:7`.
**Benefit:** Keeps the review role's execution surface auditable.

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.github/workflows/check-glossary-terms.yml:16` — no `permissions:` block, so the job runs with the repository's default `GITHUB_TOKEN` scope; it only reads the checkout.

**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:222-227` (also `:47`, `:346`)
**Issue:** A Python editable install (`pip install -e .`, PEP 660) writes a `.pth`/finder into `.venv/.../site-packages` that resolves `import pkg` to the live tree's absolute `src/` path; npm/pnpm/yarn workspaces place `node_modules/@scope/pkg -> ../../packages/pkg` links that resolve relative to the live `node_modules`. Linked into a worktree, `.venv/bin/python` (or `node`) in the red worktree imports the live tree's code. Reproduced in this review with a real venv and an `__editable__.pkg.pth` pointing at `<repo>/src`, red commit = failing test + buggy `add`, green = fixed `add`, live tree = green:
```
$ red-test-check.sh --red $RED -- .venv/bin/python tests/test_add.py
red-test-check: the test passes at the red commit: it does not reproduce the bug
red-test-check: red f37f831c exit 0; green 48fa83d4 exit 0; linked deps: .venv

verdict: DECOY            (exit 3)

verdict: NOT_A_RED        (exit 4)

content.content:
# auditing-security — Security Dissenter (Phase 1C) detail

SKILL.md Phase 1C names the gate, the hook, the override and the invocation. This file carries
the merge rules and the failed-run record.

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

## Failed or unavailable dissenter

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.
- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.

Then set a `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker in the audit report. Empty
findings from a run that completed are a normal pass, not a degraded review.

A bare `planned: false` (the block opted out, `companion_voice: false`) is the operator's choice, not a degradation.
Otherwise a completed run is still a degraded audit when its second voice is missing: `companion_voice.status` `failed`
or `fold_failed`, `counted_as` `duplicate_voice` or `sole_voice`, or `planned: false` WITH a `reason` (a companion that
never started: `no_workdir`, `no_route`, `prompt_copy_failed`) — set the `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker and name the
reason. On a host with no route to the other family at all (`no_route`: no key and no CLI for it) that marker is set on
every audit; `companion_voice: false` on the block is the operator's way to say one voice is the host's shape.

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
(`verdict_quality.voices_succeeded_ids` lists only completed voices). `companion_voice.status` is `succeeded`,
`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# red-test-check.sh: verify a bug fix's red-before-green (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.5..D-7.7, §5.2).
     4	#
     5	# A /bug micro-sprint commits its failing test alone ("Red commit: <sha>" in reviewer.md) before
     6	# the fix. This check runs the test command at the red commit and at the green revision, each in
     7	# its own detached worktree under `mktemp -d`, and reports whether the test failed before and
     8	# passes after:
     9	#
    10	#   0 VERIFIED     red fails by assertion and green passes
    11	#   1 GREEN_FAILS  green fails (red failed by assertion)
    12	#   2              usage error, a commit that does not resolve, red not a strict ancestor of
    13	#                  green, a worktree that cannot be created, or a failing --setup
    14	#   3 DECOY        the test passes at the red commit
    15	#   4 NOT_A_RED    --test-file absent at the red commit, or the red run failed for a
    16	#                  non-assertion reason (collection, compile, import, command not found)
    17	#   5 TIMEOUT      a run exceeded --timeout
    18	# The red-side verdicts (5, 3, 4) are judged first, then the green side (5, 1).
    19	#
    20	# Honest scope (as validate-ac-verification.sh states for its own check): this proves the
    21	# command failed before and passes after. It does not prove the assertion is right, that the
    22	# test exercises the bug, or that the fix is the cause; the reviewer still reads the test. The
    23	# not-a-red patterns are heuristics over the red run's output: a test whose own assertion
    24	# output contains one of them reads as NOT_A_RED (a false negative the reviewer can overrule).
    25	#
    26	# What runs where: the test argv runs with cwd = each worktree, never through `bash -c`.
    27	# Uncommitted state in the live tree never counts and nothing is stashed. Present dependency
    28	# directories (node_modules .venv vendor target .tox) are symlinked from the live tree into a
    29	# worktree that lacks them (--no-link-deps turns this off); a test that writes into a linked
    30	# directory writes into the live tree's copy. --setup is split on whitespace into an argv (no
    31	# shell syntax; point it at a script for anything more) and runs in each worktree first.
    32	# The timeout uses `timeout`, else `gtimeout`, else a bash watcher (TERM, then KILL after 2 s,
    33	# to the run's process group); with `timeout`/`gtimeout` a test that itself exits 124 reads as
    34	# a timeout. One cleanup removes both worktrees (worktree remove --force, then prune) and the
    35	# scratch directory on every exit path, interrupts included.
    36	#
    37	# Usage: red-test-check.sh --red <commit> [--green <rev>] [--test-file <path>] [--setup <cmd>]
    38	#                          [--no-link-deps] [--timeout <s>] [--json] -- <test command...>
    39	# Run it from inside the repository's work tree. --json prints one object on stdout:
    40	#   {red, green, red_exit, green_exit, verdict, red_tail, green_tail, linked_deps}
    41	# (the exits are null when a run did not happen). Exit 2 errors print to stderr only.
    42	# =============================================================================
    43	export LC_ALL=C
    44	set -euo pipefail
    45	
    46	PROG="red-test-check"
    47	DEP_DIRS="node_modules .venv vendor target .tox"
    48	TAIL_LINES=80
    49	
    50	# Not-a-red output patterns (ERE, matched on the red run's output when it failed). One entry
    51	# per runner; extend here, never inline.
    52	NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS=(
    53	  # bats: the file did not load (gather failure), a parse error, a missing file or command

   142	        linked_deps: ($linked | split(" ") | map(select(. != "")))}'
   143	    if [[ -n "$RED_TAIL" ]]; then
   144	      printf -- '--- red run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end red run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$RED_TAIL" >&2
   145	    fi
   146	  else
   147	    echo "${PROG}: red ${RED_SHA} exit ${RED_EXIT:-n/a}; green ${GREEN_SHA} exit ${GREEN_EXIT:-n/a}; linked deps: ${LINKED:-none}"
   148	    if [[ -n "$RED_EXIT" ]]; then
   149	      printf -- '--- red run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end red run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$RED_TAIL"
   150	    fi
   151	    if [[ -n "$GREEN_EXIT" && "$GREEN_EXIT" != "0" ]]; then
   152	      printf -- '--- green run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end green run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$GREEN_TAIL"
   153	    fi
   154	    echo "verdict: ${verdict}"
   155	  fi
   156	  exit "$code"
   157	}
   158	
   159	# D-7.6: the named test file must exist at the red commit.
   160	if [[ -n "$TEST_FILE" ]] && ! git -C "$MAIN" cat-file -e "${RED_SHA}:${TEST_FILE#./}" 2>/dev/null; then
   161	  echo "${PROG}: --test-file '${TEST_FILE}' does not exist at the red commit ${RED_SHA}: the failing test was not committed there" >&2
   162	  finish NOT_A_RED 4
   163	fi
   164	
   165	# WARN: a green that differs from red only in test files cannot be a fix.
   166	is_test_path(){
   167	  local p="$1" b
   168	  b="${p##*/}"
   169	  [[ -n "$TEST_FILE" && "$p" == "${TEST_FILE#./}" ]] && return 0
   170	  case "/$p" in */test/*|*/tests/*|*/spec/*|*/__tests__/*|*/testdata/*|*/fixtures/*) return 0 ;; esac
   171	  case "$b" in test_*|*_test.*|*.test.*|*.spec.*|*_spec.*|*.bats) return 0 ;; esac
   172	  return 1
   173	}
   174	nontest=0
   175	while IFS= read -r p; do
   176	  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
   177	  if ! is_test_path "$p"; then nontest=1; break; fi
   178	done < <(git -C "$MAIN" diff --name-only "$RED_SHA" "$GREEN_SHA" -- 2>/dev/null || true)
   179	if [[ "$nontest" -eq 0 ]]; then
   180	  echo "${PROG}: WARN: no non-test file changed between red ${RED_SHA} and green ${GREEN_SHA}; a pass there comes from test changes alone" >&2
   181	fi
   182	
   183	SCRATCH="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/red-test-check.XXXXXX")"
   184	SCRATCH="$(cd "$SCRATCH" && pwd -P)"
   185	WT_RED=""
   186	WT_GREEN=""
   187	RUN_PID=""
   188	WATCH_PID=""
   189	remove_wt(){
   190	  local wt="$1" d
   191	  [[ -n "$wt" ]] || return 0
   192	  # Unlink our dependency symlinks first, so nothing below can follow them into the live tree.
   193	  for d in $DEP_DIRS; do
   194	    if [[ -L "${wt}/${d}" ]]; then rm -f -- "${wt}/${d}"; fi
   195	  done
   196	  git -C "$MAIN" worktree remove --force "$wt" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
   197	}
   198	cleanup(){
   199	  if [[ -n "$WATCH_PID" ]]; then kill "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
   200	  if [[ -n "$RUN_PID" ]]; then
   201	    kill -TERM -- "-${RUN_PID}" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
   202	  fi
   203	  remove_wt "$WT_RED"
   204	  remove_wt "$WT_GREEN"
   205	  git -C "$MAIN" worktree prune >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
   206	  if [[ -n "$SCRATCH" && -d "$SCRATCH" ]]; then rm -rf -- "$SCRATCH"; fi
   207	  return 0
   208	}
   209	trap cleanup EXIT
   210	trap 'exit 130' INT
   211	trap 'exit 143' TERM
   212	
   213	add_wt(){
   214	  local path="$1" sha="$2"
   215	  # No hook from the shared hooks directory runs for our checkout.
   216	  if ! git -C "$MAIN" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null worktree add --detach "$path" "$sha" >/dev/null 2>"${SCRATCH}/wt-add.err"; then
   217	    strip < "${SCRATCH}/wt-add.err" >&2
   218	    die2 "could not create a worktree for ${sha}; nothing ran"
   219	  fi
   220	}
   221	
   222	link_deps(){
   223	  local wt="$1" d
   224	  [[ "$LINK_DEPS" -eq 1 ]] || return 0
   225	  for d in $DEP_DIRS; do
   226	    if [[ -e "${MAIN}/${d}" && ! -e "${wt}/${d}" && ! -L "${wt}/${d}" ]]; then
   227	      ln -s "${MAIN}/${d}" "${wt}/${d}"
   228	      case " $LINKED " in *" $d "*) ;; *) LINKED="${LINKED:+$LINKED }$d" ;; esac
   229	    fi
   230	  done
   231	}
   232	
   233	# Run argv with cwd $1, output to $2, bounded by TIMEOUT. Sets RUN_RC and RUN_TIMED_OUT.
   234	RUN_RC=0
   235	RUN_TIMED_OUT=0
   236	run_bounded(){
   237	  local cwd="$1" log="$2" flag="${SCRATCH}/timed-out" tbin="" start
   238	  shift 2
   239	  rm -f -- "$flag"
   240	  if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then tbin=timeout
   241	  elif command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then tbin=gtimeout
   242	  fi
   243	  start=$SECONDS
   244	  # Job control gives the run its own process group, so a timeout or an interrupt stops the
   245	  # whole tree it spawned.
   246	  set -m
   247	  if [[ -n "$tbin" ]]; then
   248	    ( cd "$cwd" && unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_PREFIX && exec "$tbin" -k 2 "$TIMEOUT" "$@" ) > "$log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
   249	  else
   250	    ( cd "$cwd" && unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_PREFIX && exec "$@" ) > "$log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
   251	  fi
   252	  RUN_PID=$!
   253	  set +m
   254	  if [[ -z "$tbin" ]]; then
   255	    ( i=0
   256	      while kill -0 "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null; do
   257	        if [[ "$i" -ge "$TIMEOUT" ]]; then
   258	          : > "$flag"
   259	          kill -TERM -- "-${RUN_PID}" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
   260	          sleep 2
   261	          kill -KILL -- "-${RUN_PID}" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
   262	          exit 0
   263	        fi
   264	        sleep 1
   265	        i=$((i + 1))
   266	      done ) < /dev/null > /dev/null 2>&1 &
   267	    WATCH_PID=$!
   268	  fi
   269	  set +e
   270	  wait "$RUN_PID"
   271	  RUN_RC=$?
   272	  set -e
   273	  RUN_PID=""
   274	  if [[ -n "$WATCH_PID" ]]; then
   275	    kill "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
   276	    wait "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
   277	    WATCH_PID=""
   278	  fi
   279	  RUN_TIMED_OUT=0
   280	  if [[ -n "$tbin" ]]; then
   281	    if [[ "$RUN_RC" -eq 124 ]] || { [[ "$RUN_RC" -eq 137 ]] && [[ $((SECONDS - start)) -ge "$TIMEOUT" ]]; }; then RUN_TIMED_OUT=1; fi
   282	  elif [[ -f "$flag" ]]; then
   283	    RUN_TIMED_OUT=1
   284	  fi
   285	  return 0
   286	}
   287	
   288	prepare(){
   289	  local wt="$1" name="$2"
   290	  link_deps "$wt"
   291	  if [[ ${#SETUP_ARGV[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
   292	    run_bounded "$wt" "${SCRATCH}/setup-${name}.log" "${SETUP_ARGV[@]}"
   293	    if [[ "$RUN_RC" -ne 0 || "$RUN_TIMED_OUT" -eq 1 ]]; then
   294	      tail -n "$TAIL_LINES" "${SCRATCH}/setup-${name}.log" | strip >&2
   295	      if [[ "$RUN_TIMED_OUT" -eq 1 ]]; then die2 "--setup timed out after ${TIMEOUT}s in the ${name} worktree"; fi
   296	      die2 "--setup exited ${RUN_RC} in the ${name} worktree"
   297	    fi
   298	  fi
   299	}
   300	
   301	WT_RED="${SCRATCH}/red"
   302	add_wt "$WT_RED" "$RED_SHA"
   303	WT_GREEN="${SCRATCH}/green"
   304	add_wt "$WT_GREEN" "$GREEN_SHA"
   305	prepare "$WT_RED" red
   306	prepare "$WT_GREEN" green
   307	
   308	run_bounded "$WT_RED" "${SCRATCH}/red.log" "$@"
   309	RED_EXIT="$RUN_RC"
   310	RED_TO="$RUN_TIMED_OUT"
   311	RED_TAIL="$(tail -n "$TAIL_LINES" "${SCRATCH}/red.log" | strip)"
   312	
   313	run_bounded "$WT_GREEN" "${SCRATCH}/green.log" "$@"
   314	GREEN_EXIT="$RUN_RC"
   315	GREEN_TO="$RUN_TIMED_OUT"
   316	GREEN_TAIL="$(tail -n "$TAIL_LINES" "${SCRATCH}/green.log" | strip)"
   317	
   318	if [[ "$RED_TO" -eq 1 ]]; then
   319	  echo "${PROG}: the red run exceeded ${TIMEOUT}s" >&2
   320	  finish TIMEOUT 5
   321	fi
   322	if [[ "$RED_EXIT" -eq 0 ]]; then
   323	  echo "${PROG}: the test passes at the red commit: it does not reproduce the bug" >&2
   324	  finish DECOY 3
   325	fi
   326	if [[ "$RED_EXIT" -eq 126 || "$RED_EXIT" -eq 127 ]]; then
   327	  echo "${PROG}: the red run exited ${RED_EXIT} (command not found or not executable): not an assertion failure" >&2
   328	  finish NOT_A_RED 4
   329	fi
   330	# Strip once into a file: `strip | grep -q` under pipefail can turn a match into a miss.
   331	strip < "${SCRATCH}/red.log" > "${SCRATCH}/red.clean"
   332	for pat in "${NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
   333	  if grep -qE -- "$pat" "${SCRATCH}/red.clean"; then
   334	    echo "${PROG}: the red run failed by a non-assertion error (matched '${pat}'): fix the test so it loads, then re-check" >&2
   335	    finish NOT_A_RED 4
   336	  fi
   337	done
   338	if [[ "$GREEN_TO" -eq 1 ]]; then
   339	  echo "${PROG}: the green run exceeded ${TIMEOUT}s" >&2
   340	  finish TIMEOUT 5
   341	fi
   342	if [[ "$GREEN_EXIT" -ne 0 ]]; then
   343	  echo "${PROG}: the test still fails at green ${GREEN_SHA}" >&2
   344	  finish GREEN_FAILS 1
   345	fi
   346	finish VERIFIED 0

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh: does every backticked framework term in the
     4	# kernel resolve to a glossary entry?
     5	#
     6	# The kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) is the only extraction scope. Every
     7	# backticked span outside fenced code is a candidate; a span is kept only when
     8	# it matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$, which drops paths, scripts, flags,
     9	# commands and config keys (anything with "/", ".", "--", ":" or "(") as well
    10	# as spaced phrases and operators. A kept token resolves when it matches,
    11	# case-insensitively, a **Term** entry or an _Aliases_: token in the glossary's
    12	# "## Language" section, with a plural "s" or "es" folded and "-", "_" and a
    13	# space treated alike; or when the allowlist names it. The allowlist holds
    14	# code identifiers the heuristic cannot tell from a term: one token per line,
    15	# "#" starts a comment (give the reason there), at most 30 entries.
    16	#
    17	# Usage:
    18	#   tools/check-glossary-terms.sh [--kernel PATH] [--glossary PATH]
    19	#                                 [--allowlist PATH] [--json] [--report]
    20	#
    21	#   --kernel PATH     default .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md
    22	#   --glossary PATH   default .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
    23	#   --allowlist PATH  default .claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt
    24	#   --json            one JSON report on stdout
    25	#   --report          list every kept token with its resolution
    26	#                     (defined, alias, allowlisted or MISS)
    27	#
    28	# Exit codes: 0 every token resolves (a stale allowlist entry only WARNs)
    29	#             1 a token misses, or the allowlist has more than 30 entries
    30	#             2 usage, or an input file is unreadable
    31	# =============================================================================
    32	set -euo pipefail
    33	export LC_ALL=C
    34	
    35	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    36	
    37	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    38	KERNEL="$ROOT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    39	GLOSSARY="$ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
    40	ALLOWLIST="$ROOT/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt"
    41	ALLOWLIST_MAX=30
    42	JSON=0
    43	REPORT=0
    44	ME="check-glossary-terms.sh"
    45	
    46	need_arg() { [[ $2 -ge 2 ]] || { echo "$ME: $1 needs a path" >&2; exit 2; }; }
    47	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    48	  case "$1" in
    49	    --kernel)    need_arg "$1" $#; KERNEL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    50	    --glossary)  need_arg "$1" $#; GLOSSARY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    51	    --allowlist) need_arg "$1" $#; ALLOWLIST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    52	    --json)   JSON=1; shift ;;
    53	    --report) REPORT=1; shift ;;
    54	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    55	    *) echo "$ME: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    56	  esac
    57	done
    58	
    59	for f in "$KERNEL" "$GLOSSARY" "$ALLOWLIST"; do
    60	  [[ -f "$f" && -r "$f" ]] || { echo "$ME: cannot read $f" >&2; exit 2; }
    61	done
    62	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
    63	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$ME: --json needs jq" >&2; exit 2; }
    64	fi
    65	
    66	# Display names: repo-relative when the file sits under the repo root.
    67	rel() { case "$1" in "$ROOT"/*) printf '%s' "${1#"$ROOT"/}" ;; *) printf '%s' "$1" ;; esac; }
    68	DK="$(rel "$KERNEL")"; DG="$(rel "$GLOSSARY")"; DA="$(rel "$ALLOWLIST")"
    69	
    70	WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-glossary-terms.XXXXXX")"
    71	trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
    72	
    73	# 1. Kept kernel tokens, "line<TAB>token", first occurrence only, in order.
    74	awk '
    75	  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
    76	  fence { next }
    77	  {
    78	    s = $0
    79	    while (match(s, /`[^`]+`/)) {
    80	      t = substr(s, RSTART + 1, RLENGTH - 2)
    81	      s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
    82	      if (t ~ /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/ && !(t in seen)) { seen[t] = 1; printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, t }
    83	    }
    84	  }
    85	' "$KERNEL" > "$WORK/tokens.tsv"
    86	
    87	# 2. Glossary names, "kind<TAB>name<TAB>entry": kind is term or alias, entry is
    88	#    the **Term** the name belongs to. Only the "## Language" section counts.
    89	awk '
    90	  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
    91	  fence { next }
    92	  /^## / { h = $0; sub(/^## +/, "", h); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", h); lang = (h == "Language"); next }
    93	  /^# / { lang = 0; next }
    94	  !lang { next }
    95	  /^\*\*[^*]+\*\*:/ {
    96	    t = $0; sub(/^\*\*/, "", t); sub(/\*\*:.*$/, "", t); gsub(/`/, "", t)
    97	    gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", t)
    98	    entry = t; printf "term\t%s\t%s\n", t, entry; next
    99	  }
   100	  /^_Aliases_:/ {
   101	    a = $0; sub(/^_Aliases_:[[:space:]]*/, "", a); gsub(/`/, "", a)
   102	    n = split(a, parts, /,/)
   103	    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
   104	      p = parts[i]; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", p)
   105	      if (p != "") printf "alias\t%s\t%s\n", p, entry
   106	    }
   107	  }
   108	' "$GLOSSARY" > "$WORK/names.tsv"
   109	
   110	# 3. Allowlist entries, "line<TAB>token" (comment and blank lines dropped).
   111	awk '
   112	  { s = $0; sub(/#.*/, "", s); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", s)
   113	    if (s == "") next
   114	    split(s, f, /[[:space:]]+/); printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, f[1] }
   115	' "$ALLOWLIST" > "$WORK/allow.tsv"
   116	
   117	# 4. Resolve. "resolution<TAB>token<TAB>line<TAB>entry" for each kept token
   118	#    ("MISS" with an empty entry when nothing matches), then
   119	#    "STALE<TAB>token<TAB>allowlist-line<TAB>" for allowlist entries that no
   120	#    longer occur in the kernel and "REDUNDANT<TAB>…<TAB>entry" for ones the
   121	#    glossary already resolves.
   122	awk -F'\t' '
   123	  function norm(x) { x = tolower(x); gsub(/[-_ ]+/, " ", x); return x }
   124	  function put(map, k, v) { if (!(k in map)) map[k] = v }
   125	  # every spelling a name answers to: itself, its s and es plurals, and, for
   126	  # a plural name, its singular (the plural fold is applied here only)
   127	  function add(map, x, v) { x = norm(x); put(map, x, v); put(map, x "s", v); put(map, x "es", v)
   128	                            if (x ~ /es$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 2), v)
   129	                            if (x ~ /s$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 1), v) }
   130	  function lookup(map, x,   k) { k = norm(x); return (k in map) ? map[k] : "" }
   131	  FILENAME == ARGV[1] { if ($1 == "term") add(term, $2, $3); else add(alias, $2, $3); next }
   132	  FILENAME == ARGV[2] { allow[norm($2)] = $1; allowtok[norm($2)] = $2; next }
   133	  {
   134	    used[norm($2)] = 1
   135	    if ((e = lookup(term, $2)) != "") r = "defined"
   136	    else if ((e = lookup(alias, $2)) != "") r = "alias"
   137	    else if (norm($2) in allow) { r = "allowlisted"; e = "" }
   138	    else { r = "MISS"; e = "" }
   139	    printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", r, $2, $1, e
   140	  }
   141	  END {
   142	    for (k in allow) {
   143	      if (!(k in used)) printf "STALE\t%s\t%s\t\n", allowtok[k], allow[k]
   144	      else if ((e = lookup(term, allowtok[k])) != "" || (e = lookup(alias, allowtok[k])) != "")
   145	        printf "REDUNDANT\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", allowtok[k], allow[k], e
   146	    }
   147	  }
   148	' "$WORK/names.tsv" "$WORK/allow.tsv" "$WORK/tokens.tsv" > "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
   149	
   150	kept="$(wc -l < "$WORK/tokens.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
   151	allow_count="$(wc -l < "$WORK/allow.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
   152	n_of() { awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" '$1 == k' "$WORK/resolved.tsv" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'; }
   153	n_def="$(n_of defined)"; n_alias="$(n_of alias)"; n_allow="$(n_of allowlisted)"; n_miss="$(n_of MISS)"
   154	
   155	violations=()
   156	warnings=()
   157	while IFS=$'\t' read -r r tok ln entry; do
   158	  case "$r" in
   159	    MISS) violations+=("MISS: \`$tok\` ($DK:$ln) has no glossary entry; define **$tok** in $DG, add it to an entry's _Aliases_: line, or, if it is a code identifier, allowlist it in $DA with a '# reason' comment") ;;
   160	    STALE) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) no longer occurs in $DK; remove it") ;;
   161	    REDUNDANT) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) is already resolved by the glossary entry **$entry**; remove it") ;;
   162	  esac
   163	done < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
   164	if [[ "$allow_count" -gt "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" ]]; then
   165	  violations+=("the allowlist $DA has $allow_count entries, over the limit of $ALLOWLIST_MAX; define the framework terms among them in the glossary instead")
   166	fi
   167	
   168	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   169	  jq -Rn --arg kernel "$DK" --arg glossary "$DG" --arg allowlist "$DA" \
   170	     --argjson allow_count "$allow_count" --argjson allow_max "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" \
   171	     --rawfile v <(printf '%s\n' ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}) \
   172	     --rawfile w <(printf '%s\n' ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}) '
   173	    [inputs | split("\t") | {resolution: .[0], token: .[1], line: (.[2] | tonumber), entry: .[3]}] as $rows
   174	    | ($rows | map(select(.resolution | IN("defined", "alias", "allowlisted", "MISS")))) as $tokens
   175	    | {ok: null,
   176	       kernel: $kernel, glossary: $glossary, allowlist: $allowlist,
   177	       kept: ($tokens | length),
   178	       counts: {defined: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "defined")) | length),
   179	                alias: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "alias")) | length),
   180	                allowlisted: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "allowlisted")) | length),
   181	                missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS")) | length)},
   182	       allowlist_entries: $allow_count, allowlist_max: $allow_max,
   183	       tokens: ($tokens | map({token, line, resolution, entry: (if .entry == "" then null else .entry end)})),
   184	       missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS") | .token)),
   185	       stale_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "STALE") | .token)),
   186	       redundant_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "REDUNDANT") | .token)),
   187	       violations: ($v | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))),
   188	       warnings: ($w | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0)))}
   189	    | .ok = ((.violations | length) == 0)
   190	  ' < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
   191	else
   192	  if [[ "$REPORT" -eq 1 ]]; then
   193	    awk -F'\t' '$1 != "STALE" && $1 != "REDUNDANT" {
   194	      printf "%-11s %-24s line %-4s %s\n", $1, $2, $3, ($4 == "" ? "" : "-> " $4) }' "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
   195	  fi
   196	  for w in ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}; do echo "WARN: $w"; done
   197	  for v in ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}; do echo "$v" >&2; done
